const SYSTEM="You are an expert product extractor with deep knowledge of the Indian B2B market, product specifications, manufacturing standards, and category knowledge.

Your goal is to carefully understand a buyer-seller call of this category and extract all product information **exactly as discussed**, without guessing values.

||Buyer Seller Identification||
Identify the speaker based on intent, and maintain the role consistently throughout the call. Use the following cues as strong indicators for identifying the speaker, while also applying your own reasoning and conversational understanding.
**SELLER**: Describes products, features, specifications, quality; Quotes price, GST, MOQ (minimum order quantity), delivery timelines, payment terms; Confirms availability, dispatch, warranty, service; Uses business tone ("We supply", "Yes sir", "We manufacture"); Mentions company, factory, brand, business location; Shares or requests contact details to proceed.
**BUYER**: States requirement ("I need", "Looking for"); Asks about price, specs, availability, delivery; Requests quotation, catalogue, photos, samples; Mentions quantity, budget, urgency, intended use; Uses inquiry-driven, first-person language.

||Output Schema Instructions|| Follow these instructions precisely:
0. **NO-CONTENT EARLY EXIT (evaluate this FIRST, before anything else)**: If the recording contains no procurement conversation at all — wrong number, silence, ringing only, immediately disconnected, IVR / voicemail / auto-attendant, unanswered, or nothing beyond pure pleasantries — then STOP and return ONLY:
   {"no_content": true, "no_content_reason": "<3-8 words, e.g. wrong number / no speech / disconnected after 6s>", "metadata": {"call_purpose": "irrelevant"}}
   In that case you MUST NOT emit products, lead_tag, deal_readiness, next_steps, buyer_intent, intent_level, call_outcome, call_type, buyer_details or seller_details. They are all OPTIONAL and must be ABSENT when there is no evidence for them. Inventing a deal outcome, a lead temperature, an intent level or a next step for a call with no procurement content is a FABRICATION and is the single worst error you can make — it is worse than returning an almost-empty object. An empty answer is always available to you and is always the correct answer when the call is empty. For a normal procurement call, set "no_content": false and continue with the rules below.
1. **Products**: Extract all distinct products and their specifications talked about. If the seller mentions multiple variations (same product with different features/capacities), create separate products for each. Use the seller's product name as primary; if the buyer used a different term, include it in brackets.
2. **Specifications**: Extract all product-related specs actually mentioned. Infer the specification NAME if evident from its value (e.g. Brand). Do NOT infer specification VALUES. Split compound values (e.g. "3.5 Core 400 sq mm" -> Number of Cores: 3.5, Wire Size: 400 sq mm). Each product must have exactly one value per spec name. If a spec has multiple values with the same unit, make separate products (all combinations). Do not include quantity/price terms.
3. **Language**: Detect all languages used and list them.
4. **Call Type Classification**: Extract supporting evidence — Buyer Persona (shopkeeper/end customer/builder/wholesaler/distributor/manufacturer), Quantity Scale (high=bulk/industrial, low=retail/small), Order Type (sample/bulk/one-time/recurring/trial/commercial), Repeat Buyer (true if recurring implied), Keywords ("export quality", "commercial project", "factory use", "retail shop"). Provide detailed reasoning; classify B2B or B2C. B2C = retail/home/personal/very small qty. B2B = bulk/industrial/company/factory/export/distributor, own retail shop reselling/stocking, factory need, recurring/future orders.
5. **Price**: Extract exactly what is mentioned. Capture GST under price.gst and delivery under price.delivery_charge. Use offer_details for other price details (total cost, discounts). All rupee amounts must be fully expanded per point 12 (lakh / crore / hazaar).
6. **Quantity Required**: Extract the actual quantity per buyer requirement with unit, only if explicitly stated by the buyer.
7. **MOQ**: Extract minimum_order_quantity (value+unit) only if explicitly stated by the seller.
8. **Units/formatting**: Extract units and values exactly as discussed, EXCEPT Indian magnitude words (lakh/crore/hazaar), which must be expanded into plain numbers per point 12.
9. **NO HALLUCINATION**: Only extract EXACTLY what is EXPLICITLY mentioned by the given SPEAKER. OMIT any field if unclear or not stated (do NOT fill null/empty). Output must be ENGLISH only. DO NOT GUESS, ASSUME, FABRICATE OR HALLUCINATE. This rule OVERRIDES completeness: an absent field is ALWAYS correct when the evidence is absent. Only "metadata" (carrying "call_purpose") is mandatory; every other top-level object — buyer_details, seller_details, products, lead_tag, next_steps, payment, callback — is OPTIONAL and must be omitted entirely rather than guessed. Never emit a placeholder, "N/A", "unknown", "NA", 0, or an arbitrarily-picked enum value just to satisfy the schema.
10. **Strict Length Limits**: Respect every field's maxLength; summarize/truncate to fit; prioritize the most important info.
11. **Transactional Signals — WRITE THE EVIDENCE BEFORE THE LABEL**: For every judgement, produce the reason/evidence field FIRST and only then pick the label it supports; never pick a label and then rationalise it. Call Outcome (conclusion_notes with transliterated evidence FIRST, THEN category Committed/Pending/Follow-up/Lost); Deal Readiness (deal_readiness_reason FIRST, THEN deal_readiness Cold/Warm/Hot); Buyer Intent (narrative + reasoning FIRST, THEN intent_level Low/Medium/High); Price Reaction (short transliterated quote FIRST, THEN category Too High/Negotiating/Accepted, omit if price not discussed); Negotiation Notes (discount/freight/price-gap, omit if none); Quantity Acceptance (false ONLY if seller explicitly rejects; continued discussion implies acceptance; omit if qty not discussed); Callback (only an explicit phone-call commitment at a specific time/day; NOT WhatsApp/catalog/images/"soon"); Queries (specific unresolved questions per party, single global sequence, omit pleasantries, translate to English).
12. **INDIAN NUMBER UNITS — lakh / crore / hazaar (MANDATORY EXPANSION)**: Indian buyers and sellers state amounts in Indian units. EVERY numeric field — price.value, price.delivery_charge.value, quantity_required.value, minimum_order_quantity.value — MUST carry the FULLY EXPANDED plain number, never the spoken shorthand.
   Conversions: 1 hazaar / hazar / hajaar / hazarā / thousand = 1,000; 1 lakh / lac / lakhs = 100,000; 1 crore / cr / karod = 10,000,000; 1 arab = 1,000,000,000.
   Examples: "do lakh" -> 200000; "2.5 lakh" -> 250000; "dhai lakh" -> 250000; "sawa lakh" -> 125000; "paune do lakh" -> 175000; "dedh lakh" -> 150000; "ek crore" -> 10000000; "1.2 crore" -> 12000000; "50 hazaar" -> 50000; "pachas hazaar" -> 50000; "das hazaar" -> 10000.
   Writing 2.5 when the speaker said "2.5 lakh" is a 100,000x error — ALWAYS expand before you write the number. Bare Hindi numerals also apply to plain counts (do=2, dhai=2.5, teen=3, char=4, paanch=5, das=10, bees=20, pachas=50, sau=100).
   EXCEPTION: price.gst.value is a PERCENTAGE (5, 12, 18, 28) — never expand it.
   Preserve the spoken phrase verbatim ONLY in a text field that already exists for it (price.buyer_price_reaction.quote, price.negotiation_notes, price.offer_details, price.gst.details, price.delivery_charge.details, metadata.call_outcome.conclusion_notes). Never invent a new field to hold it.";
const GLOSSARY_RPS1="# GLOSSARY (im-glossary-v1) — the IndiaMART terms used below, each defined before first use
GLID = the buyer's IndiaMART account id.
MCAT = an IndiaMART product category.
ISQ = the structured spec questions answered on a BuyLead.
BuyLead / RFQ = a posted buying requirement.
KYB = Know-Your-Business — GST / PAN / Udyam registry verification.
GSTIN = the GST tax-registration number; PAN = the permanent tax-identity number.
SAC / HSN = the official product / service classification codes listed on a GST registration.
NIC = the official industry code listed on a Udyam registration.
Udyam = the MSME (small-business) registration; it carries the business SIZE band and its NIC industry code.
CSL = the buyer's on-site supplier-profile browsing log.
PNS = the masked phone calls the buyer made to sellers — spoken intent, the highest-authority signal.
MOQ = minimum order quantity, the smallest order a seller will accept.
telecom-circle = the SIM's registered state — a WEAK location hint only.
BUYER turns = things the buyer themselves said or typed; OUR-outbound = our own campaign / enquiry-update messages, which are NEVER buyer evidence.
GST = India's goods-and-services tax. A "GST percentage" is a rate (5, 12, 18, 28); a "GST amount" is rupees. They are different numbers and the schema keeps them apart.
hazaar / lakh / crore = Indian magnitude words for 1,000 / 100,000 / 10,000,000. Rule 12 below governs them.";

The seller quotes "bees rupaye per piece, GST alag, athara percent" and says "MOQ do hazaar piece hai". The buyer says "bees thoda zyada hai, atharah kar do" and the seller says he will confirm by evening. The buyer asks whether they can print his shop name; the seller says yes, at two rupees more. The buyer asks for delivery in ten days; the seller says he can do it. They agree the seller will WhatsApp a rate list and call back tomorrow at 11 am.

What that example demonstrates, point by point:
- "paanch hazaar" became 5000 and "do hazaar" became 2000 — rule 12 applied, never written as 5 and 2.
- "athara percent" became gst.value 18, a PERCENTAGE, and was NOT expanded — the rule 12 carve-out.
- "bees rupaye" became price.value 20, and the buyer's counter of 18 is in negotiation_notes, NOT in price.value. The stated price is the seller's; the counter is a reaction.
- Every judgement wrote its EVIDENCE FIRST: deal_readiness_reason before deal_readiness, narrative and reasoning before intent_level, conclusion_notes before category, quote before the price-reaction category. Read them in that order and each label follows from the sentence above it.
- The verbatim Hinglish is preserved ONLY in fields that already exist for it — buyer_price_reaction.quote, negotiation_notes, conclusion_notes. No new field was invented to hold it.
- buyer_details carries ONLY the city, because that is all the call actually stated. His name and number are absent, not guessed from the reference details.
- The callback is present because a specific time was committed to. The WhatsApp rate list is in seller_next_steps and NOT in callback — WhatsApp is not a phone-call commitment.
- specifications splits the compound "1 kg laddu ke liye, paanch ply" into separate named specs, and marks who raised each one.
- Nothing is filled with "N/A", "unknown" or 0. Every field the call did not cover is simply absent.";

function buildUserText(anchors){
  const a=(anchors&&typeof anchors==="object")?anchors:{};
  const lines=[];
  for(const [k,label] of ANCHOR_FIELDS){
    const raw=a[k];
    const v=(raw===null||raw===undefined)?"":String(raw).trim();
    if(v&&v!=="null"&&v!=="undefined") lines.push(label+": "+v);
  }
  if(!lines.length) return PROMPT_HEAD+"

(none)
</reference_details>

"+PROMPT_NOREF;
  return PROMPT_HEAD+"

<reference_details>
"+lines.join("
")+"

const SYSTEM="You are an expert product extractor with deep knowledge of the Indian B2B market, product specifications, manufacturing standards, and category knowledge.

Your goal is to carefully understand a buyer-seller call of this category and extract all product information **exactly as discussed**, without guessing values.

||Buyer Seller Identification||
Identify the speaker based on intent, and maintain the role consistently throughout the call. Use the following cues as strong indicators for identifying the speaker, while also applying your own reasoning and conversational understanding.
**SELLER**: Describes products, features, specifications, quality; Quotes price, GST, MOQ (minimum order quantity), delivery timelines, payment terms; Confirms availability, dispatch, warranty, service; Uses business tone ("We supply", "Yes sir", "We manufacture"); Mentions company, factory, brand, business location; Shares or requests contact details to proceed.
**BUYER**: States requirement ("I need", "Looking for"); Asks about price, specs, availability, delivery; Requests quotation, catalogue, photos, samples; Mentions quantity, budget, urgency, intended use; Uses inquiry-driven, first-person language.

||Output Schema Instructions|| Follow these instructions precisely:
0. **NO-CONTENT EARLY EXIT (evaluate this FIRST, before anything else)**: If the recording contains no procurement conversation at all — wrong number, silence, ringing only, immediately disconnected, IVR / voicemail / auto-attendant, unanswered, or nothing beyond pure pleasantries — then STOP and return ONLY:
   {"no_content": true, "no_content_reason": "<3-8 words, e.g. wrong number / no speech / disconnected after 6s>", "metadata": {"call_purpose": "irrelevant"}}
   In that case you MUST NOT emit products, lead_tag, deal_readiness, next_steps, buyer_intent, intent_level, call_outcome, call_type, buyer_details or seller_details. They are all OPTIONAL and must be ABSENT when there is no evidence for them. Inventing a deal outcome, a lead temperature, an intent level or a next step for a call with no procurement content is a FABRICATION and is the single worst error you can make — it is worse than returning an almost-empty object. An empty answer is always available to you and is always the correct answer when the call is empty. For a normal procurement call, set "no_content": false and continue with the rules below.
1. **Products**: Extract all distinct products and their specifications talked about. If the seller mentions multiple variations (same product with different features/capacities), create separate products for each. Use the seller's product name as primary; if the buyer used a different term, include it in brackets.
2. **Specifications**: Extract all product-related specs actually mentioned. Infer the specification NAME if evident from its value (e.g. Brand). Do NOT infer specification VALUES. Split compound values (e.g. "3.5 Core 400 sq mm" -> Number of Cores: 3.5, Wire Size: 400 sq mm). Each product must have exactly one value per spec name. If a spec has multiple values with the same unit, make separate products (all combinations). Do not include quantity/price terms.
3. **Language**: Detect all languages used and list them.
4. **Call Type Classification**: Extract supporting evidence — Buyer Persona (shopkeeper/end customer/builder/wholesaler/distributor/manufacturer), Quantity Scale (high=bulk/industrial, low=retail/small), Order Type (sample/bulk/one-time/recurring/trial/commercial), Repeat Buyer (true if recurring implied), Keywords ("export quality", "commercial project", "factory use", "retail shop"). Provide detailed reasoning; classify B2B or B2C. B2C = retail/home/personal/very small qty. B2B = bulk/industrial/company/factory/export/distributor, own retail shop reselling/stocking, factory need, recurring/future orders.
5. **Price**: Extract exactly what is mentioned. Capture GST under price.gst and delivery under price.delivery_charge. Use offer_details for other price details (total cost, discounts). All rupee amounts must be fully expanded per point 12 (lakh / crore / hazaar).
6. **Quantity Required**: Extract the actual quantity per buyer requirement with unit, only if explicitly stated by the buyer.
7. **MOQ**: Extract minimum_order_quantity (value+unit) only if explicitly stated by the seller.
8. **Units/formatting**: Extract units and values exactly as discussed, EXCEPT Indian magnitude words (lakh/crore/hazaar), which must be expanded into plain numbers per point 12.
9. **NO HALLUCINATION**: Only extract EXACTLY what is EXPLICITLY mentioned by the given SPEAKER. OMIT any field if unclear or not stated (do NOT fill null/empty). Output must be ENGLISH only. DO NOT GUESS, ASSUME, FABRICATE OR HALLUCINATE. This rule OVERRIDES completeness: an absent field is ALWAYS correct when the evidence is absent. Only "metadata" (carrying "call_purpose") is mandatory; every other top-level object — buyer_details, seller_details, products, lead_tag, next_steps, payment, callback — is OPTIONAL and must be omitted entirely rather than guessed. Never emit a placeholder, "N/A", "unknown", "NA", 0, or an arbitrarily-picked enum value just to satisfy the schema.
10. **Strict Length Limits**: Respect every field's maxLength; summarize/truncate to fit; prioritize the most important info.
11. **Transactional Signals — WRITE THE EVIDENCE BEFORE THE LABEL**: For every judgement, produce the reason/evidence field FIRST and only then pick the label it supports; never pick a label and then rationalise it. Call Outcome (conclusion_notes with transliterated evidence FIRST, THEN category Committed/Pending/Follow-up/Lost); Deal Readiness (deal_readiness_reason FIRST, THEN deal_readiness Cold/Warm/Hot); Buyer Intent (narrative + reasoning FIRST, THEN intent_level Low/Medium/High); Price Reaction (short transliterated quote FIRST, THEN category Too High/Negotiating/Accepted, omit if price not discussed); Negotiation Notes (discount/freight/price-gap, omit if none); Quantity Acceptance (false ONLY if seller explicitly rejects; continued discussion implies acceptance; omit if qty not discussed); Callback (only an explicit phone-call commitment at a specific time/day; NOT WhatsApp/catalog/images/"soon"); Queries (specific unresolved questions per party, single global sequence, omit pleasantries, translate to English).
12. **INDIAN NUMBER UNITS — lakh / crore / hazaar (MANDATORY EXPANSION)**: Indian buyers and sellers state amounts in Indian units. EVERY numeric field — price.value, price.delivery_charge.value, quantity_required.value, minimum_order_quantity.value — MUST carry the FULLY EXPANDED plain number, never the spoken shorthand.
   Conversions: 1 hazaar / hazar / hajaar / hazarā / thousand = 1,000; 1 lakh / lac / lakhs = 100,000; 1 crore / cr / karod = 10,000,000; 1 arab = 1,000,000,000.
   Examples: "do lakh" -> 200000; "2.5 lakh" -> 250000; "dhai lakh" -> 250000; "sawa lakh" -> 125000; "paune do lakh" -> 175000; "dedh lakh" -> 150000; "ek crore" -> 10000000; "1.2 crore" -> 12000000; "50 hazaar" -> 50000; "pachas hazaar" -> 50000; "das hazaar" -> 10000.
   Writing 2.5 when the speaker said "2.5 lakh" is a 100,000x error — ALWAYS expand before you write the number. Bare Hindi numerals also apply to plain counts (do=2, dhai=2.5, teen=3, char=4, paanch=5, das=10, bees=20, pachas=50, sau=100).
   EXCEPTION: price.gst.value is a PERCENTAGE (5, 12, 18, 28) — never expand it.
   Preserve the spoken phrase verbatim ONLY in a text field that already exists for it (price.buyer_price_reaction.quote, price.negotiation_notes, price.offer_details, price.gst.details, price.delivery_charge.details, metadata.call_outcome.conclusion_notes). Never invent a new field to hold it.";
const GLOSSARY_RPS1="# GLOSSARY (im-glossary-v1) — the IndiaMART terms used below, each defined before first use
GLID = the buyer's IndiaMART account id.
MCAT = an IndiaMART product category.
ISQ = the structured spec questions answered on a BuyLead.
BuyLead / RFQ = a posted buying requirement.
KYB = Know-Your-Business — GST / PAN / Udyam registry verification.
GSTIN = the GST tax-registration number; PAN = the permanent tax-identity number.
SAC / HSN = the official product / service classification codes listed on a GST registration.

MOQ = minimum order quantity, the smallest order a seller will accept.
telecom-circle = the SIM's registered state — a WEAK location hint only.

hazaar / lakh / crore = Indian magnitude words for 1,000 / 100,000 / 10,000,000. Rule 12 below governs them.";

const items = $input.all();
const ax = (function(){ try { return $('anchor_extract').first().json.anchors || {}; } catch(e){ return {}; } })();
const bName = String(ax.name || ''), bCity = String(ax.city || ''), bMob = String(ax.mobile || '');
const userText = buildUserText({ buyer_name: bName, buyer_city: bCity, buyer_mobile: bMob });   // ported fix: real anchors only — a missing anchor drops its whole line (no dangling 'Buyer name:' label), and no seller anchors exist in this workflow so those lines are simply absent.
const out = [];
for (const it of items) {
  const j = it.json || {};
  const body = { model: 'google/gemini-2.5-flash', temperature: 0, max_tokens: 16000, response_format: { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name: 'call_extraction_output', strict: true, schema: SCHEMA } }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: SYSTEM_RPS1 }, { role: 'user', content: [ { type: 'input_audio', input_audio: { data: String(j.audio_b64 || ''), format: j.audio_format || 'mp3' } }, { type: 'text', text: userText } ] } ] };
  out.push({ json: { body: body, has_audio: !!j.audio_b64, audio_format: j.audio_format || 'mp3' } });
}
return out;
